newsitem.title: USA: Clorox says sales growth boosts net income.
newsitem.headline: Clorox says sales growth boosts net income.

text.p: The Clorox Co. said Wednesday its profits climbed 13 percent in its fiscal fourth quarter, driven by strong sales growth for its household cleaning products.
The Oakland, Calif.-based company said net income rose to $74.4 million, or $1.44 a share for the quarter ended June 30, compared with $65.8 million, or $1.28 a share in the same period a year ago.
The results surpassed analysts' average forecast of $1.38 a share, and the company's stock rallied $2.875to $137.50 in composite afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
Sales climbed to $762.5 million from $672.5 million in the year-ago quarter.
Clorox said it ended the fiscal year with profits of $249.4 milllion, an increase of 12 percent from $222.1 million in 1996.

Fuelling the rise in earnings were record-level shipments for the quarter and the year, cost-saving initiatives and improved profit margins in its U.S. and international operations. The growth occurred despite the company's acquisition last December of Armour All Products, which reduced earnings by 8 cents a share in the fourth quarter and 11 cents on the year.
Clorox is the maker of household and automotive cleaning products and the Brita walter filtration system.
